extraction.name: Video-MME: The First-Ever Comprehensive Evaluation Benchmark of Multi-modal LLMs in Video Analysis
extraction.description: Video-MME is the first-ever full-spectrum, Multi-Modal Evaluation benchmark of MLLMs in Video analysis. It consists of 900 videos spanning 6 primary visual domains with 30 subfields, ranging from 11 seconds to 1 hour in duration. The dataset includes 2,700 high-quality multiple-choice questions (3 per video) annotated by expert annotators. It integrates multi-modal inputs including video frames, subtitles, and audios to evaluate the comprehensive capabilities of Multimodal Large Language Models.
extraction.creator: Chaoyou Fu, Yuhan Dai, Yongdong Luo, Lei Li, Shuhuai Ren, Renrui Zhang, Zihan Wang, Chenyu Zhou, Yunhang Shen, Mengdan Zhang, Peixian Chen, Yanwei Li, Shaohui Lin, Sirui Zhao, Ke Li, Tong Xu, Xiawu Zheng, Enhong Chen, Caifeng Shan, Ran He, Xing Sun
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset construction involves three main steps: video collection, question-answer annotation, and quality review. Videos were sourced from YouTube across 6 key domains (Knowledge, Film & Television, Sports Competition, Life Record, Multilingual) and 30 fine-grained categories. Raw videos were collected with varying durations (short, medium, long). Subtitles and audios were obtained where available. Annotators with strong English proficiency and research experience created 3 multiple-choice QA pairs per video. A rigorous manual review process was conducted, including cross-verification by different annotators and filtering out questions answerable via text-only using Gemini 1.5 Pro.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw videos sourced from YouTube, along with associated subtitles and audio tracks.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Videos were categorized into short (<2 minutes), medium (4-15 minutes), and long (30-60 minutes). QA pairs were filtered to ensure they required video content as a critical clue; questions answerable solely based on text were removed using Gemini 1.5 Pro. Subtitles were synchronized with sampled video frames for evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators with strong English proficiency and extensive research experience in vision-language learning were recruited. Each annotator viewed the entire video and iteratively created three multiple-choice questions, each with four candidate options. A rigorous manual review process was conducted where each QA pair was examined by a different annotator to verify clarity, logical consistency, and appropriateness of the correct answer. Additionally, text-only questions were tested against Gemini 1.5 Pro to filter out those that did not require video content.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Statistical analysis showed that Gemini 1.5 Pro achieved less than 15% accuracy in the text-only setup, underscoring the robustness of the video content-based requirement. The distribution of options (A/B/C/D) followed a near-uniform distribution (25.1/27.2/25.3/22.4%), ensuring an unbiased evaluation.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotators were selected for having strong English proficiency and extensive research experience in vision-language learning.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Gemini 1.5 Pro was used to filter out QA pairs that could be answered solely based on textual questions.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark underscores the need for further improvements in handling longer sequences and multimodal data, shedding light on future MLLM development. It highlights that image understanding is the basis of video understanding and reveals gaps between commercial and open-source models.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset covers 6 visual domains and 30 subfields, but may not represent all real-world scenarios. Performance of MLLMs declines as video duration increases, indicating limitations in processing longer sequences. Open-source models generally lag behind commercial models. The evaluation relies on multiple-choice questions which may not capture all aspects of video understanding.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) for video understanding. It is designed to evaluate capabilities in perception, reasoning, and information synthesis across varying temporal contexts and modalities.
